frases.texto: Don Quixote of La Mancha. Part 3: The Sierra Morena and Princess Micomicona
frases.fala: Don Quixote of La Mancha. Part 3: The Sierra Morena and Princess Micomicona

frases.texto: With the gleaming helmet he won in the rain and a heart brimming over with dreams, the Knight of the Sorrowful Face climbs with Sancho into the wild and mighty mountains of the SIERRA MORENA!
frases.fala: With the gleaming helmet he won in the rain and a heart brimming over with dreams, the Knight of the Sorrowful Face climbs with Sancho into the wild and mighty mountains of the sierra morena!

frases.texto: High among the rocks, between cliffs, pine trees and wild flowers, our heroes will open a suitcase full of secrets, write a moving love LETTER, turn somersaults of longing and discover a clever plan by old friends to rescue a beautiful PRINCESS from a faraway kingdom.
frases.fala: High among the rocks, between cliffs, pine trees and wild flowers, our heroes will open a suitcase full of secrets, write a moving love letter, turn somersaults of longing and discover a clever plan by old friends to rescue a beautiful princess from a faraway kingdom.

frases.texto: Take a deep breath of the fresh mountain air, turn the page and climb the sierra with them!
frases.fala: Take a deep breath of the fresh mountain air, turn the page and climb the sierra with them!

frases.texto: Chapter 16. The Lost Suitcase. A Treasure in the Middle of the Mountains
frases.fala: Chapter 16. The Lost Suitcase. A Treasure in the Middle of the Mountains

frases.texto: Climbing the stony mountain paths, between twisted holm oaks and steep crags, Sancho tripped over a mysterious SUITCASE of tanned leather, abandoned under a prickly bush.
frases.fala: Climbing the stony mountain paths, between twisted holm oaks and steep crags, Sancho tripped over a mysterious suitcase of tanned leather, abandoned under a prickly bush.

frases.texto: The suitcase was worn out by time, soaked by the rains and shut tight with rusty clasps.
frases.fala: The suitcase was worn out by time, soaked by the rains and shut tight with rusty clasps.

frases.texto: What could that forgotten case be hiding?
frases.fala: What could that forgotten case be hiding?

frases.texto: Open the suitcase with a tap to uncover its secret!
frases.fala: Open the suitcase with a tap to uncover its secret!

frases.texto: Inside it gleamed dozens of precious gold COINS, which made Sancho’s eyes sparkle with pure delight, and a dainty NOTEBOOK full of POEMS written in elegant handwriting.
frases.fala: Inside it gleamed dozens of precious gold coins, which made Sancho’s eyes sparkle with pure delight, and a dainty notebook full of poems written in elegant handwriting.

frases.texto: “Gold, my lord!
frases.fala: Gold, my lord!

frases.texto: Real gold!” cheered Sancho, hopping up and down.
frases.fala: Real gold! cheered Sancho, hopping up and down.

frases.texto: Don Quixote took the notebook in his hands with the greatest respect and read aloud the tender verses of a young man in love who wandered lost through the mountains.
frases.fala: Don Quixote took the notebook in his hands with the greatest respect and read aloud the tender verses of a young man in love who wandered lost through the mountains.

frases.texto: “Whoever writes with such feeling has a noble soul,” said the gentleman with a fond sigh.
frases.fala: Whoever writes with such feeling has a noble soul, said the gentleman with a fond sigh.

frases.texto: “Books hold the deepest mysteries of the human heart!”
frases.fala: Books hold the deepest mysteries of the human heart!

frases.texto: Chapter 17. The Somersaults of Longing. A Knight Head over Heels
frases.fala: Chapter 17. The Somersaults of Longing. A Knight Head over Heels

frases.texto: Gazing at the vast loneliness of the mountains, Don Quixote had a shining idea: “Friend Sancho, I shall stay in this clearing to show the whole world my great LONGING for Dulcinea, fasting and pondering just as the famous hero AMADIS of Gaul once did!
frases.fala: Gazing at the vast loneliness of the mountains, Don Quixote had a shining idea: Friend Sancho, I shall stay in this clearing to show the whole world my great longing for Dulcinea, fasting and pondering just as the famous hero amadis of Gaul once did!

frases.texto: And you shall ride off on your donkey to carry a loving letter into her very hands.”
frases.fala: And you shall ride off on your donkey to carry a loving letter into her very hands.

frases.texto: “But, my noble master,” asked Sancho, scratching his chin, “how shall I convince the lady Dulcinea that your grace nearly lost your wits for her, if I don’t see some astonishing deed with my own eyes?”
frases.fala: But, my noble master, asked Sancho, scratching his chin, how shall I convince the lady Dulcinea that your grace nearly lost your wits for her, if I don’t see some astonishing deed with my own eyes?

frases.texto: “Then see one right now!” cried Don Quixote firmly.
frases.fala: Then see one right now! cried Don Quixote firmly.

frases.texto: He took off his iron armour and, wearing nothing but his long white nightshirt, turned a quick SOMERSAULT on the grass and kicked his skinny legs up into the air in mid-leap!
frases.fala: He took off his iron armour and, wearing nothing but his long white nightshirt, turned a quick somersault on the grass and kicked his skinny legs up into the air in mid-leap!

frases.texto: Sancho covered his face with both hands, laughing so hard that tears ran down his cheeks.
frases.fala: Sancho covered his face with both hands, laughing so hard that tears ran down his cheeks.

frases.texto: Help the knight with his acrobatics of love!
frases.fala: Help the knight with his acrobatics of love!

frases.texto: Chapter 18. The Letter for Dulcinea. Sancho Forgot the Letter!
frases.fala: Chapter 18. The Letter for Dulcinea. Sancho Forgot the Letter!

frases.texto: Deeply moved, Don Quixote wrote a beautiful LETTER to his beloved on a page torn from the poetry notebook, full of poetic words and his solemn promise to be faithful for ever.
frases.fala: Deeply moved, Don Quixote wrote a beautiful letter to his beloved on a page torn from the poetry notebook, full of poetic words and his solemn promise to be faithful for ever.

frases.texto: He gave his instructions to his trusty squire, who climbed onto his donkey and set off down the road, feeling like the most important person in all of Spain!
frases.fala: He gave his instructions to his trusty squire, who climbed onto his donkey and set off down the road, feeling like the most important person in all of Spain!

frases.texto: But as he rode down the first slopes, Sancho put his hands in his pockets and his eyes grew wide with panic: he had left the paper on a rock high up in the mountains!
frases.fala: But as he rode down the first slopes, Sancho put his hands in his pockets and his eyes grew wide with panic: he had left the paper on a rock high up in the mountains!

frases.texto: In despair, he scratched his forehead and tried to bring back the words kept only in his MEMORY: “How did it begin again?
frases.fala: In despair, he scratched his forehead and tried to bring back the words kept only in his memory: How did it begin again?

frases.texto: ‘Sovereign and exalted lady’...
frases.fala: ‘Sovereign and exalted lady’...

frases.texto: And at the end?
frases.fala: And at the end?

frases.texto: How did he sign it again?”
frases.fala: How did he sign it again?

frases.texto: Help the good squire remember the SIGNATURE on the letter by tapping each word in the right order!
frases.fala: Help the good squire remember the signature on the letter by tapping each word in the right order!

frases.texto: Chapter 19. Friends in Disguise. The Priest, the Barber and an Ox-Tail Beard
frases.fala: Chapter 19. Friends in Disguise. The Priest, the Barber and an Ox-Tail Beard

frases.texto: Stopping at an inn at the foot of the mountain, Sancho met two dear old friends from his village: the kind PRIEST Pero Pérez and Master Nicolás, the village barber.
frases.fala: Stopping at an inn at the foot of the mountain, Sancho met two dear old friends from his village: the kind priest Pero Pérez and Master Nicolás, the village barber.

frases.texto: Worried because their friend Alonso Quixano had vanished, they had come ready to rescue him with loving care.
frases.fala: Worried because their friend Alonso Quixano had vanished, they had come ready to rescue him with loving care.

frases.texto: “He will never agree to come home of his own free will,” warned Sancho, “unless a damsel in distress begs for the protection of his unbeatable sword!”
frases.fala: He will never agree to come home of his own free will, warned Sancho, unless a damsel in distress begs for the protection of his unbeatable sword!

frases.texto: “I know!” cried the priest, his eyes shining.
frases.fala: I know! cried the priest, his eyes shining.

frases.texto: “Let’s invent a princess in distress!”
frases.fala: Let’s invent a princess in distress!

frases.texto: And so the two of them hatched a brilliant, theatrical plan: a cunning DISGUISE!
frases.fala: And so the two of them hatched a brilliant, theatrical plan: a cunning disguise!

frases.texto: Master Nicolás stuck an enormous reddish BEARD on his chin, made from the hairy tail of an ox, while the priest put on a swirly skirt and a flowery bonnet over his cassock.
frases.fala: Master Nicolás stuck an enormous reddish beard on his chin, made from the hairy tail of an ox, while the priest put on a swirly skirt and a flowery bonnet over his cassock.

frases.texto: When they looked at themselves in the inn’s mirror, all three burst out laughing, so breathless they could hardly carry on with the play-acting!
frases.fala: When they looked at themselves in the inn’s mirror, all three burst out laughing, so breathless they could hardly carry on with the play-acting!

frases.texto: Chapter 20. Princess Micomicona. A Princess Asks for Help
frases.fala: Chapter 20. Princess Micomicona. A Princess Asks for Help

frases.texto: To make the plan perfect, they were joined by Dorotea, a clever, fearless young country girl with a wonderful talent for acting.
frases.fala: To make the plan perfect, they were joined by Dorotea, a clever, fearless young country girl with a wonderful talent for acting.

frases.texto: Dressed in a shimmering silk gown and a velvet cloak, she climbed up into the mountains and knelt gracefully before the gentleman:
frases.fala: Dressed in a shimmering silk gown and a velvet cloak, she climbed up into the mountains and knelt gracefully before the gentleman:

frases.texto: “O mirror of honour and flower of chivalry!” she pleaded in a velvety voice.
frases.fala: O mirror of honour and flower of chivalry! she pleaded in a velvety voice.

frases.texto: “I am the unhappy PRINCESS MICOMICONA, heiress to the faraway kingdom of Micomicón!
frases.fala: I am the unhappy princess micomicona, heiress to the faraway kingdom of Micomicón!

frases.texto: A fierce and heartless giant, Pandafilando of the Gloomy Glare, has invaded my lands, and only your brave arm can set my people free!”
frases.fala: A fierce and heartless giant, Pandafilando of the Gloomy Glare, has invaded my lands, and only your brave arm can set my people free!

frases.texto: Deeply moved, Don Quixote held out his hand to the damsel and made a sacred PROMISE: “Rise, fair princess!
frases.fala: Deeply moved, Don Quixote held out his hand to the damsel and made a sacred promise: Rise, fair princess!

frases.texto: I swear by my sword that I shall defeat that giant!”
frases.fala: I swear by my sword that I shall defeat that giant!

frases.texto: And so, with his mind full of celebration and his heart full of nobility, the gentleman climbed onto Rocinante and, without suspecting a thing, set off on the road back to his own home!
frases.fala: And so, with his mind full of celebration and his heart full of nobility, the gentleman climbed onto Rocinante and, without suspecting a thing, set off on the road back to his own home!

frases.texto: Chapter 21. The Battle of the Wineskins. A Giant in the Middle of the Night
frases.fala: Chapter 21. The Battle of the Wineskins. A Giant in the Middle of the Night

frases.texto: On the way home, they all stayed at the inn, and the night was passing peacefully when battle cries woke the whole house: “Surrender, you cowardly monster!
frases.fala: On the way home, they all stayed at the inn, and the night was passing peacefully when battle cries woke the whole house: Surrender, you cowardly monster!

frases.texto: Taste my steel!”
frases.fala: Taste my steel!

frases.texto: Don Quixote, sleepwalking in his long white nightshirt, was fighting a fierce battle against the big WINESKINS of ox hide, full of red wine, that hung on the walls of the room!
frases.fala: Don Quixote, sleepwalking in his long white nightshirt, was fighting a fierce battle against the big wineskins of ox hide, full of red wine, that hung on the walls of the room!

frases.texto: Lost in his vivid DREAM, he saw every hanging wineskin as the dreadful GIANT Pandafilando!
frases.fala: Lost in his vivid dream, he saw every hanging wineskin as the dreadful giant Pandafilando!

frases.texto: Swinging his sharp SWORD in the dark, he pierced the thick leather and sent a river of sweet-smelling wine pouring across the floorboards like a crimson waterfall.
frases.fala: Swinging his sharp sword in the dark, he pierced the thick leather and sent a river of sweet-smelling wine pouring across the floorboards like a crimson waterfall.

frases.texto: Tap the sword to help the knight defeat the wineskins!
frases.fala: Tap the sword to help the knight defeat the wineskins!

frases.texto: “My wine!
frases.fala: My wine!

frases.texto: My wine!” wailed the innkeeper in despair.
frases.fala: My wine! wailed the innkeeper in despair.

frases.texto: “Calm down, my good man, I shall pay for every drop!” promised the generous priest.
frases.fala: Calm down, my good man, I shall pay for every drop! promised the generous priest.

frases.texto: And Don Quixote, wiping the sweat from his brow with childlike pride, lay down again in peace, quite sure that he had saved Princess Micomicona’s throne!
frases.fala: And Don Quixote, wiping the sweat from his brow with childlike pride, lay down again in peace, quite sure that he had saved Princess Micomicona’s throne!

frases.texto: Chapter 22. Arms and Letters. Stories at the Inn
frases.fala: Chapter 22. Arms and Letters. Stories at the Inn

frases.texto: That cosy night, the great hall of the inn filled up with travellers, merchants and families around a big table lit by torches and sweet-scented candles.
frases.fala: That cosy night, the great hall of the inn filled up with travellers, merchants and families around a big table lit by torches and sweet-scented candles.

frases.texto: Warm bread was passed from hand to hand, and each traveller shared wonderful STORIES of adventures at sea, surprise reunions and ancient legends from all over the world.
frases.fala: Warm bread was passed from hand to hand, and each traveller shared wonderful stories of adventures at sea, surprise reunions and ancient legends from all over the world.

frases.texto: At one point, Don Quixote stood up at the head of the table and gave a wise and moving speech about the worth of ARMS and LETTERS: “The courage of knights protects the peace and defends the weak.
frases.fala: At one point, Don Quixote stood up at the head of the table and gave a wise and moving speech about the worth of arms and letters: The courage of knights protects the peace and defends the weak.

frases.texto: And books, my friends, make justice, truth and beauty grow in our hearts!”
frases.fala: And books, my friends, make justice, truth and beauty grow in our hearts!

frases.texto: All the listeners looked at one another in amazement, surprised to discover the shining wisdom that lived inside that kind-eyed gentleman.
frases.fala: All the listeners looked at one another in amazement, surprised to discover the shining wisdom that lived inside that kind-eyed gentleman.

frases.texto: The priest and the barber smiled, deeply touched: it was time to take that dear dreamer back to the comfort of his home!
frases.fala: The priest and the barber smiled, deeply touched: it was time to take that dear dreamer back to the comfort of his home!
